candidates.name: 600-cell (CW complex on S^3)
candidates.notes: f-vector (120,720,1200,600) gives chi=0 (S^3). 2I left-multiplication on the unit icosians is free.

candidates.name: S^3
candidates.notes: Closed odd-dim manifold, chi=0 by Poincare duality.

candidates.name: S^3/2I  (Poincare sphere)
candidates.notes: Free 2I quotient of S^3; chi = 0/120 = 0. Same conclusion for S^3/2T, S^3/2O and any S^3/cyclic.

candidates.name: S^4
candidates.notes: chi=2.  Any smooth finite-group action on S^4 has fixed points (e.g. 2I via SO(5) representation has fixed antipodal points), so the quotient is an orbifold, not a manifold.

candidates.name: CP^2
candidates.notes: chi=3.  Aut(CP^2) = PGL(3,C); finite subgroups classified (Hambleton-Lee).  A_5 = 2I/Z_2 embeds in PGL(3,C) but the lift to 2I has fixed points; not free.

candidates.name: K3
candidates.notes: chi(K3)=24. Mukai (1988) classified finite groups acting symplectically on K3: max group is M_23-stabilizers, |G| <= 960, and 2I = SL(2,5) of order 120 IS one of the 11 maximal Mukai groups. BUT every non-trivial finite symplectic action on K3 has fixed points (Nikulin 1979), so 24/120 = 1/5 is NOT an integer and the quotient is an orbifold. Resolving the orbifold gives an Enriques-type or rational surface, not a CY threefold.

candidates.name: K3 / 2I  (orbifold)
candidates.notes: Mukai-type quotient.  24/120 is non-integer => fixed points => orbifold. Crepant resolutions (when they exist) inflate chi back up; resolved smooth manifold is not CY_3 in any case.

candidates.name: Tian-Yau CY_3  (Z/3 quotient of quintic-related CICY)
candidates.notes: Free Z/3 quotient.  h^11=14, h^21=23  =>  chi = 2(14-23) = -18? Original Tian-Yau (1987) reports chi=-6 for the Z/3-free quotient of the bicubic; |chi|/2 = 3 generations. NO 2I-symmetry: |Aut| is small, dominated by the Z/3 used in the quotient.

candidates.name: CICY-7884  (3-generation CY_3)
candidates.notes: From the Candelas et al. CICY list; chi=-6 via discrete-group quotient of an ambient CICY by a small abelian group.  No icosahedral / H_4 symmetry.

candidates.name: Z/5 x Z/5  free quotient of quintic
candidates.notes: Free (Z/5)^2 quotient of the Fermat quintic gives chi = -200/25 = -8, not -6.  No 2I action.

candidates.name: CY_3 with H_4 symmetry  (hypothetical)
candidates.notes: H_4 is a non-crystallographic Coxeter group of order 14400 acting on R^4. It does NOT preserve any integer lattice in dim<=8 [Patera-Twarock 2002].  No CY_3 with a faithful H_4 action is known in the literature.  H_4 lifts to E_8 via the icosian construction, but this is a SYMMETRY OF THE LATTICE, not of any compact manifold of complex dim 3.

candidates.name: 600-cell / I  (icosahedral 600-cell)
candidates.notes: 3-manifold of the form S^3/H; chi=0.  Cannot give chirality.

summary.obstruction_summary: (1) chi(S^3/H)=0 for ALL finite H acting freely on S^3, so any product with a chi=0 partner stays at chi=0; (2) the only 2I-type action on K3 is non-free (Mukai/Nikulin), yielding orbifolds with non-integer chi/|G|; (3) no CY_3 with chi=+/-6 is known to admit a 2I or H_4-coloured action, because H_4 is non-crystallographic and CY_3 automorphism groups are typically abelian or small.

references_master: Conway-Sloane 1999 'Sphere Packings, Lattices and Groups' ch.8
